## Session of 2026-10-21, 18:46–20:40 (U1–U7): whether experience is constituted by interpretation, grounding kept apart from it, and which entries it bears on

*2026-10-21 21:27:23*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-136 CLAIM-155 CLAIM-165 CLAIM-196 CLAIM-198 CLAIM-342 CLAIM-355 CLAIM-368 CLAIM-411 CLAIM-412 CLAIM-413 THEORY-043 THEORY-044 THEORY-056 THEORY-063 THEORY-064 THEORY-095 THEORY-101 THEORY-507 THEORY-577 THEORY-633 THEORY-680 THEORY-767 THEORY-769 — Proposed; claims, questions and readings cited as open, nothing here rests on their being settled -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1343 — Deferred; works registered unread, cited as such -->
*Reconstructed on 2026-10-21, at the owner's request, from the shared
exchange "Experience And Interpretation"
(https://chatgpt.com/share/6ad92c62-4dd0-83e9-9056-fcffd5957cf2), which ran
on 2026-10-21 with owner turns from 18:46 to 20:40 UTC. Owner turns are
U1–U7, counted without the "custom instructions" placeholder. A1–A7 is the
reply to each. Where a reply was streamed in parts, the longest copy
contains every other part and is canonical. A5 was preceded by repository
reads through a connector, which are not reconstructed here. Nothing
reached the repository from the exchange itself. Times are UTC.*

**Shape.** Seven owner turns. The owner's thesis (U1) and choice of
reading with three examples (U2). Two requests for related research (U3,
U6). A question about two positions (U4). A request to connect the
exchange to this record (U5). A request for a synthesis (U7). It started
from a premise about grounding and became a constitutive thesis about
experience. Its recurring strength was keeping that thesis apart from what
the evidence shows: each reply said what its examples motivate and what
they do not establish. Its recurring weakness was the usual one, works and
positions proposed as new that the record already holds. Before U5 the
replies had not seen the record, so what they did not use is listed as
on file, not as missed.

- **U1 (18:46): "i think it's reasonable to posit that a necessary
  condition for *grounded* experience is sensory apparatus. … it further
  follows from this line of reasoning that experience is fundamentally an
  interpretive act. this line of reasoning admittedly leaves the binding
  problem begging, but invites reframing questions about the possibility
  of experience as questions about the possibility of forming judgements
  and interpretations. thoughts?"** The owner's thesis. A1 split it into
  three claims and said that neither the second nor the third "follows
  deductively from the first". It made grounding relational ("grounding is
  fundamentally relational, whereas interpretation can, in principle, be
  internally realized"). It moved the centre from judgement to
  "interpretive organization". It recast binding as "What organizational
  conditions allow multiple informational processes to participate in a
  unified interpretive perspective?" It closed on the fork: is experience
  "*constituted by* interpretation", or is interpretation "the mechanism
  that *produces* experience"? **Right:** the separation of grounding,
  experience and interpretation, which the record now holds as two claims.
  It was also right to flag the cost of identifying experience with
  interpretation, that it "risk[s] making experience ubiquitous". **Filed:**
  the thesis with U2, as [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md); the grounding premise as
  [CLAIM-413](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md). **Not filed:** the "conceptual continuum" figure,
  which A1 itself captioned as "not an established ordering".
- **U2 (19:08): "yeah former reading. relevant ideas: brain in a vat,
  rubber hand illusion, cbt"**. The owner's choice of the constitutive
  reading, and three examples. A2: "Experience may be the enactment of an
  interpretation, rather than the reception of information about the
  world." It tabulated what each example varies, wrote
  \(E_t = \mathcal I(S_{\le t}, M_t, C_t)\) with the identity reading ("The
  ongoing realization of \(\mathcal I\) … is the experience"), and asked
  whether the experiencer is constituted too. **Right:** the CBT caveat,
  that a causal reading fits its success as well; and Putnam's
  externalism as a complication for the vat. **On file:** the rubber hand
  illusion is a cluster read on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20. Botvinick and
  Cohen is [LIT-1277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md). [THEORY-766](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md) (Active) separates referred touch,
  ownership and drift, which A2's "The experience of ownership itself
  changes" ran together. A5 later corrected this. CBT's two readings are
  [THEORY-056](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-056.md) and [THEORY-680](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-680.md). **Filed:** in [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md), with the
  examples set out as evidence for construction, not constitution.
  Putnam's chapter registered unread ([LIT-1343](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1343.md)). **Not filed:** the
  formula as a formula. The claim states the identity in words.
- **U3 (20:01): "is our discussion currently in conversation with any
  contemporary cognitive science, neurology, or philosophy research we
  should take into consideration?"** A request. A3 surveyed active
  inference, constructed emotion, representationalism and higher-order
  theories, enactivism, neurological cases (Charles Bonnet,
  somatoparaphrenia, reappraisal) and the COGITATE result. It named the
  "most serious challenge": "Interpretation ⇏ Conscious experience",
  because unconscious systems interpret continually. It separated three
  theses: content is interpretively constructed (A); experience is
  constituted by interpretive organization (B); the organization can be
  realized without sensory or biological embodiment (C). It ended on "What
  differentiates an interpretation that merely processes information from
  an interpretation that constitutes a perspective?" **Right:** A against
  B against C, and its grounding table (current, developmental,
  functional). **On file:** COGITATE ([LIT-973](../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md)), Barrett's 2017 statement
  of constructed emotion ([LIT-542](../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md)), Seth's interoceptive inference
  ([THEORY-767](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md)), demand characteristics in the rubber hand illusion
  ([LIT-1276](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1276.md), [LIT-1280](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1280.md)), and the no-report and access readings on
  [QUESTION-048](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md). **Filed:** the challenge as [CLAIM-411](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md), a counter;
  the closing question as [QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md); six works registered unread
  (the curation entry of 2026-10-21). **Not filed:** the Charles Bonnet
  review and the somatoparaphrenia source, which A3 cited without a title
  or author; the philosophers it named without a work (Tye, Dretske,
  Kriegel, Mendelovici, Rosenthal, Varela, Thompson, Noë, O'Regan).
- **U4 (20:07): "how does illusionism fit in? structural realism?"** A
  question. A4: illusionism makes the apparently intrinsic qualities of
  experience themselves interpretive constructions; structural realism
  makes relations, not intrinsic natures, what is real or knowable. It
  proposed three positions: phenomenal structural realism, illusionism,

  MEG study, a functional workspace in language models, two objections
  (Aldé on similarity structuralism; minimal-content meditation), and
  current work on the brain-in-a-vat premise. **Right:** its main
  conclusion, against itself: "we should therefore not present
  interpretive constitution or relational individuation themselves as
  novel without further qualification"; its caution on the sheaf paper
  ("compatible local sections … need not establish that there exists a
  conscious subject"); and its four independence theses. **Missed:**
  - Luppi et al. 2024 is [LIT-949](../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), already held. Only the 2026 paper is
    new;
  - the record's own gluing account of a self ([CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md), Active;
    [CLAIM-196](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)–[CLAIM-198](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md)), which A6 referred to only as "existing work on
    contextuality, gluing". It is where the sheaf paper would land.

  corrected: the paper's title ends "(HCH)". The grounding independence
  theses are in [CLAIM-413](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md). **Not filed:** the R, U, G, M framework
  of four dimensions, which A6 said must not become "a scalar function"
  and which [CASE-114](../../record/cases.d/CASE-114.md)'s note now carries in part; the reading-priority
  table.
- **U7 (20:39): "lay out our current synthesis and then flesh it out
  further"**. A request. A7 named the view "Structural-Interpretive
  Constitution (SIC)" and set it out in seven theses: ontological,
  organizational, structural, grounding, selfhood, epistemic, and an
  "open sufficiency condition". It defined interpretation and
  perspectival organization without experience, and gave a formal sketch

  **Right:** the bridge between perspectival organization and experience

  itself establish graded phenomenality", and its reading of [CLAIM-368](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md),
  that frustration "need not involve felt distress". **Missed:**
  - its binding decomposition is partly on file. [CLAIM-355](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) records the
    exchange of 2026-10-17's five bindings, and that the framework

  - its "self is not required" is [THEORY-063](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md)'s claim, as at U5;
  - its "Study B" is [CASE-114](../../record/cases.d/CASE-114.md), which A7 did cite, plus a converse arm.

  [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md). The open sufficiency condition is [CLAIM-411](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md). The
  grounding thesis, with the semantic-externalism qualification, is in
  [CLAIM-413](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md). The unity point is [QUESTION-255](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md), set against
  [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md). Study B's converse arm is in the note on [CASE-114](../../record/cases.d/CASE-114.md). **Not
  filed:**
  - the name "SIC", which A7 itself gave "Not because we've established a
    theory of consciousness";
  - the formal sketch, whose property \(\mathsf P\) is unspecified;
  - Studies A and C, which name kinds of evidence and no design;
  - the whirlpool analogy, which A7 said "cannot demonstrate that
    consciousness is organizational";
  - the rival-hypothesis table, a summary of positions the record reads
    elsewhere.

**What the exchange did for the record.** The evidence-for-experience line
had two questions, one claim and two cases. It had no thesis about what
experience is, only about what it is not shown to be ([CLAIM-355](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md),
[CLAIM-165](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md)). The owner's U1 and U2 give it one, [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md), with its
objection beside it ([CLAIM-411](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md)) and the question that would answer
the objection ([QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md)). The owner's grounding premise, through
A5's "Ungrounded ≠ Unconstrained", connects this line to the
distributed-agency line's [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md), which no entry had done.
[QUESTION-255](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) puts the record's gluing account of a self against
phenomenal unity for the first time. Most of the positions the replies
surveyed were already read here or are now registered. The record's
contribution was the owner's: keeping constitution, grounding and
self-attribution as separate questions.

## Session of 2026-10-22, 00:08–01:08 (U8–U11): formalizing perspective, the record's machinery for it, and what a perspective and an interpretation are

*2026-10-22 01:18:06*

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-22, at the owner's request, from the same shared
exchange as the entry of 2026-10-21, "Experience And Interpretation", as
reshared with four more owner turns
(https://chatgpt.com/share/6ad9632a-0f50-83ea-85af-deea963492c6). U1–U7
and A1–A7 are unchanged and are not repeated here. U8–U11 ran on
2026-10-22 from 00:08 to 01:08 UTC. Where a reply was streamed in parts,
the longest copy contains every other part and is canonical. A9 was
preceded by repository reads through a connector, and A10 by computation,
neither reconstructed here. A10 also reported a working note,
"perspectival_organization_v0_2.md", in the exchange's sandbox, which the
share does not carry and the record does not hold. Nothing reached the
repository from the exchange itself. Times are UTC.*

**Shape.** Four owner turns: a go-ahead to formalize (U8), a request to
look further into the record (U9), a go-ahead to build on what was found
(U10), and a question going back to first terms (U11). The exchange moved
from a new formalism (A8) to the record's existing one (A9–A10), and then
back to definitions (A11). U9 turned it. A9: "Nucleation's work on causal
sufficiency, self-maintaining constraints, and the meaning–authority loop
already supplies much of the technical machinery we were trying to invent
for perspectival organization." U11 caught the slide the formalism had
made possible. A11: "we've become much more precise about the organization
of interpretation without fully clarifying what the organization is
supposed to constitute." The recurring strength was retraction on
evidence: A9 withdrew most of A8, and A11 withdrew part of A10. The
recurring weakness, before U9, was building from scratch what the record
already held.

- **U8 (00:08): "go for it"**. A go-ahead for A7's offer to formalize
  perspective. A8 proposed "Perspectival Organization 0.1". A shared frame
  z_t constrains local interpretations and is updated by them. It named
  four candidate properties (contextual interpretation, endogenous
  relevance, reciprocal integration, temporal continuity), kept grounding
  and self-modelling apart, and built a frame as a class of histories
  equivalent under intervention. It added a reciprocity test, a partition
  test (Γ_τ, Jensen–Shannon), cross-context answerability, unity as
  "jointly consequential interpretation, not necessarily ... agreement",
  a two-process toy model, a five-condition definition of a "perspectival
  regime", and a three-architecture test (aggregation, external
  synchronization, reciprocal recontextualization). **Right:** the XOR
  point, "Information integration and perspectival integration are not the
  same property"; that Γ_τ "measures causal interdependence, not
  phenomenality"; the negative control, a module that only declares unity;
  and its own limit: "A sophisticated thermostat could exhibit similar
  mathematics." **Missed, before it looked:**
  - the history-equivalence frame is [TERM-062](../../record/terms.d/TERM-062.md)'s causal state, which A9 then
    found;
  - [CLAIM-330](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) makes reciprocity yield self-confirming capture;
  - [CLAIM-407](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md) shows that predictive closure is not interventional
    adequacy.

  **Filed:** cross-context answerability and unity-as-organized-conflict
  in [TERM-072](../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md) and in notes of 2026-10-22 on [QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md) and
  [QUESTION-255](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md); the three-architecture test as a design, in the note
  on [QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md). **Not filed:** the definition of a perspectival
  regime and its biconditional, which A9 replaced and A11 revised; Γ_τ,
  which A8 itself called "a diagnostic instrument rather than a
  consciousness metric"; the toy model, of which A8 said a thermostat could
  share the mathematics.
- **U9 (00:20): "judging from the direction you've gone with your
  formalization, I think there might be more content on the nucleation
  record worth connecting to or building on top of. poke around a bit more
  and see what you can find."** A request. A9 found the record's
  individuation and will-organization machinery and rebuilt A8 on it. It

  the warning. It turned [CLAIM-330](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) against A8's reciprocity. It disciplined
  the sheaf use with [CLAIM-197](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md), [CLAIM-143](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md) and [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md), and gave
  significance a form in [CLAIM-347](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s compatibility complex and [CLAIM-365](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)'s
  residual. It required the evaluation regime to be declared first
  ([TERM-065](../../record/terms.d/TERM-065.md), [CLAIM-152](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md), [CLAIM-350](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md), [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md)), and replaced a score with a
  profile ([QUESTION-252](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md)). It mapped [CASE-099](../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), [CASE-101](../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md), [CASE-110](../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md), [CASE-114](../../record/cases.d/CASE-114.md)
  and [CASE-125](../../record/cases.d/CASE-125.md) onto tests, and split the work into an organizational and a

  Its turn against itself is sound: "Reciprocal integration is a
  description of an organizational mechanism, not necessarily a distinctive

  where the interpretation–authority loop closes between institutions, and

  the question's two halves; its sheaf constraints in the note on
  [QUESTION-255](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md). **Not filed:**

  - the profile Π_ℛ, which is [QUESTION-115](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md)'s and [QUESTION-252](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md)'s approach,
    not a new one;

- **U10 (00:48): "make it so"**. A go-ahead. A10, "Perspectival
  Organization 0.2", put the perspective in the joint operator dynamics and
  separated four properties: representation, efficacy, endogenous
  allocation and constitutive maintenance. It built two constructions to

  (SMIR), to be evaluated under [TERM-065](../../record/terms.d/TERM-065.md) and [TERM-067](../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md). **Right:** both

  and one fast dependence, which A10 built without citing. Also right: its

  that the four facts come apart and only intervention separates them,
  with [CASE-126](../../record/cases.d/CASE-126.md). **Not filed:**

    [TERM-072](../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md) keeps as a subclass;

- **U11 (01:08): "circling back to some of the obstacles we encountered
  earlier in this discussion, under our current characterization what is a
  perspective? an interpretation?"** A question. A11: "An interpretation
  is a context-dependent determination of significance. A perspective is
  an organized, dynamically maintained system of relationships through
  which interpretations acquire, contest, and revise their significance."

  (perspective, three senses and a subclass), both Proposed, since adoption

**What the session did for the record.** U8–U11 made no new reading
necessary. Every result it relied on was the record's: the operator model,
the response profile, closure of constraints, the capture instability and
the frustration complex. What it added was a use for them. They are now
the tests any organizational criterion for a perspective must pass
([QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md), note of 2026-10-22). It added one demonstrated result,
[CLAIM-414](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md). And at the owner's U11 it added the distinction that keeps
the constitutive thesis honest: an organizational perspective is not yet a
phenomenal one, and [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) is the claim that some are.

## Session of 2026-10-22, 02:08–05:59 (U1–U19): choosing manuscripts from the record's graph, the competition that redirected it, and the cases the owner asked for

*2026-10-22 10:38:20*

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-22, at the owner's request, from the shared
exchange "Graph Learning Applications"
(https://chatgpt.com/share/6ad9dfd2-3ed0-83e9-9abe-4e12e94cbdd7), which
ran on 2026-10-22 with forty owner turns from 02:08 to 09:48 UTC. This
entry covers U1–U19; the entry that follows covers U20–U40. Owner turns
are counted without the "custom instructions" placeholder, and A1–A19 is
the reply to each. Where a reply was streamed in parts, the longest copy
contains every other part and is canonical. A2 was cut off after its
preamble when the owner sent U3 two minutes later. Most replies were
preceded by repository reads through a connector, and A6 by running rules
over the record's fact graph; those reads are not reconstructed here.
Every record code the replies cited was checked against the record, and
A6's rules were re-run in clingo against `luria facts`. Nothing reached
the repository from the exchange itself. Times are UTC.*

**Shape.** Nineteen owner turns in two movements. In the first (U1–U11)
the owner asked how graph methods could pick manuscripts from the record,
and steered by correction: use the record's arguments as test material,
not as software requirements (U3); luria already builds the fact graph
(U6); search forward from questions and backward from claims (U8); use
the generated chain views (U10). In the second (U12–U19) the owner
pointed the work at a competition, asserted that the whole record was
eligible for it (U13), and asked for essays, syntheses and cases. The
recurring strength was the replies' accuracy about the record's
structure: of the 133 codes cited, every relation, status and warrant
checked was right but four. The recurring weakness was the usual one at
a larger scale: theses proposed as new that the record already holds,
and papers proposed that the exchange of 2026-10-20 had already proposed
(workbench of 2026-10-21, 02:56, Papers A–F).

  of graph representation learning to github.com/dmarx/nucleation. one

  [CLAIM-183](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md), that generated views become instruments of the argument,
  which A1's programme presupposes.

## Branch of the same session, 09:27–16:18 (B37–B39): the doorway effect and the Cultural Revolution as interruptions of a perspective, perspective and agency, and a review of this record's filing of the session

*2026-10-22 16:33:52*

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-22, at the owner's request, from a branch of the
exchange "Graph Learning Applications", shared as "Branch · Graph Learning
Applications" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6ada3a18-6ee8-83ea-8255-9b4a91b2a86a).
The branch is identical to the original through U36 and A36 (entries of
2026-10-22, 10:38:20 and 10:38:21). It then replaces U37–U40 of the
original with three owner turns of its own, numbered here B37–B39, at
09:27, 11:33 and 16:18 UTC. B39 asked for a review of the pull request
that filed the original exchange, and B39's reply read the branch of the
record through a connector. Where a reply was streamed in parts, the
longest copy is canonical. Nothing reached the repository from the
exchange itself. Times are UTC.*

**Shape.** Two substantive turns and a review. The owner brought two new
cases at once (B37), asked the question the perspective account had
deferred (B38), and asked whether the record's filing of the session
needed changes (B39). The replies again found the record's own entries
for what they built ([TERM-055](../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md), [TERM-044](../../record/terms.d/TERM-044.md), [TERM-063](../../record/terms.d/TERM-063.md), [NOTE-352](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md), [THEORY-688](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md)),
and A-B39 checked the filing against the record's terms and found three
errors in it.

- **B37 (09:27): "I think we also may have landed on a likely (at least
  partial) simple, high-level explanation (or at the very least intuition)
  for The Doorway Effect (i.e. connect perspective and grounded
  experience). Also, another potentially interesting case to examine in
  the neighborhood of the martial arts material is the (various)
  perspectival interruption(s) caused by the Chinese Cultural
  Revolution."** The owner's intuition and a new case. The reply found
  "an important missing dimension": the conditions under which a
  perspective "remains available, not merely the conditions under which it
  is acquired or reproduced". It read the doorway effect through event
  segmentation ("an inaccessible intention is not necessarily an erased
  intention"), kept its failed replications, found the record's K-lines
  ([NOTE-352](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md)) and doorway options ([THEORY-688](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md)), and split interruption into
  activation, enactment and reproduction. For the Cultural Revolution it
  set out four interruptions, from "The teacher remains, but teaching
  becomes dangerous" to "Reconstruction becomes a new source of
  authenticity", from Su's study of Shaolin. **Right:** "That isn't yet a
  new scientific explanation"; "our theory shouldn't reduce perspective to
  location", from the return-to-the-room result; and "The human costs are
  morally central." **Missed:** [CLAIM-413](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md), the record's claim that
  grounding is a relation apart from whether an experience occurs, which
  the reply's "grounding isn't merely where a perspective was acquired"
  extends. **Wrong:** the classic paper's subtitle is "experienced space",
  not "mental space"; Su's study is a 2016 article, reprinted as a 2019
  chapter. **Filed:** the kinds of interruption as [CLAIM-421](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md); the
  question as [QUESTION-257](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-257.md); the doorway effect as [CASE-136](../../record/cases.d/CASE-136.md) and
  the Chinese martial traditions as [CASE-139](../../record/cases.d/CASE-139.md); six works registered
  unread. **Not filed:** a 2026 virtual-reality study and a taijiquan
  study the reply cited without identifying them; the four stipulated
  cases ("The Forgotten Errand" and the rest), whose contrasts are in the
  question and the case.
- **B38 (11:33): "what's the relationship between perspective and
  agency?"** A question. The reply: "Perspective concerns how a situation
  becomes meaningful and actionable. Agency concerns how an organized
  system can make a difference to what happens." It found the record's
  two criteria of agency ([TERM-044](../../record/terms.d/TERM-044.md), Active; [TERM-063](../../record/terms.d/TERM-063.md), Proposed) and noted
  "there may be no theory-neutral answer". It separated a perspective from
  an agent, agency from the exercise of a perspective, and first-order
  agency from perspectival regulation and reflexive governance, and laid
  out four arrangements of agents and perspectives. **Right:** keeping
  [TERM-072](../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md) free of self-maintenance so that agency stays a question; "the
  second half seems substantially safer". It used the record's
  [CLAIM-275](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md), that action can come before the interpretation it makes
  available, for the reciprocal half. It also used [CLAIM-388](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md), that a coherent
  collective variable need not be a bounded agent. **Filed:** the safer half as [CLAIM-418](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md); its closing
  question as [QUESTION-260](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-260.md), refining [QUESTION-093](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md). **Not filed:** "Every
  sufficiently rich exercise of agency involves an organization of
  practical significance", which the reply qualified at once; the
  "reciprocally constituting" thesis, which it said "deserves caution".
- **B39 (16:18): "the following PR reflects an attempt to update the
  record to reflect the progress we've made through our discussion and
  how our ideas have evolved and matured. is there anything you think we
  should change or add?"** with a link to the pull request. The reply
  judged that the filing "largely preserves the conceptual progress
  accurately" and asked for targeted changes. **Right, and acted on the
  same day:**
  - [TERM-045](../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s note had Clive Wearing failing sense 3 "as remembered
    continuity". Sense 3 is persistence, and the case shows why
    persistence must not be identified with remembered continuity. The
    note is corrected.
  - [CLAIM-417](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) and [TERM-072](../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md)'s note read a realized perspective as lying
    in one carrier. A perspective may be realized across several carriers
    at once, where integration across them can be shown. Both now leave
    that open.
  - [CLAIM-417](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) turned narrative, presented and modeled selves into
    representations of a perspective. They may describe a perspective,
    attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, and a narrative self
    can represent a person's history. The claim is narrowed.
  - [CASE-133](../../record/cases.d/CASE-133.md) and the note on [CLAIM-329](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) said the parties' perspective
    did not persist. Some orientations persisted, others moved, and the
    parties' perspectives were heterogeneous throughout. Both are
    narrowed.
  - [CLAIM-424](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md) attributed reflexive governance to a perspective; it
    belongs to a perspective-bearing organization. The title is narrowed.
  - [CASE-138](../../record/cases.d/CASE-138.md) implied one unchanged cause; the board's finding is a
    recurrence of related mechanisms. The title is narrowed.
  - [CLAIM-423](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) should not make timescale a source of authority, and
    [CLAIM-416](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-416.md) should allow success to generalize where capacities do.
    Both gained a qualification.
  - The documented cases resting on unread works ([CASE-130](../../record/cases.d/CASE-130.md),
    [CASE-135](../../record/cases.d/CASE-135.md)) now say that their standing is the event's, not the
    reading's.

  It also asked for the perspective–agency question and the interruption
  question, which are filed above. It suggested a follow-up pull request
  for them; they are filed in the same one, since the owner asked for this
  branch to be accounted for in it.

**What the branch did for the record.** It added a temporal dimension the
perspective account lacked, availability as distinct from existence, with
one cognitive and one historical case, and it put agency beside
perspective without settling which criterion of agency the record uses.
Its review caught three places where the filing had conflated what the
session took care to separate: persistence with memory, a perspective
with one carrier, and a party's organization with a single perspective.

(https://chatgpt.com/share/6adc1ece-bb28-83e9-a8f6-cadf0f8b7113). The
owner's turns U1–U27 ran from 2026-10-23, 17:07, to 2026-10-24, 02:45,
UTC; A_n is the reply to U_n. Where a reply was streamed in parts, the
longest copy contains the others and is canonical. Many replies were

**Shape.** Three reviews of PR [#327](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/327) (U1–U3); an audit of the will and
affect lines (U4–U5); then one long line of construction from a single
owner observation, that wanting is a prediction under do() (U6). It ran
through skills and amortization (U8–U12), cycles (U13), anxiety (U14–U15),
protectionism (U16), toy models (U17), legibility (U18–U22), hedonic
drive, feeling and belief (U23–U26), and back to the pragmatic-transport
line (U27). Most of the turns that turned the exchange were the owner's
short redirections: "a formalization of anxiety" (U14), "we already have a
three variable system somewhere" (U18), "forget about that distinction"
(U27). The replies' recurring strength was scoping: each candidate claim
came with the alternative explanation it had to beat and the evidence it
did not have. Their recurring weakness was proposing new machinery before
looking for the record's; U18 caught the clearest instance.

**What the exchange did for the record.** It gave the will line a
mechanism it lacked: a learned prior over who governs, with the condition
under which it amortizes and the condition under which it entrenches. It
turned that entrenchment into a candidate account of anxiety and of
protective institutions, and found the record's own [CASE-124](../../record/cases.d/CASE-124.md) to be the
model of both once the owner pointed to it. It filed two objections to
[CLAIM-440](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) and applied the third review that PR [#327](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/327) had left unapplied. It
closed by connecting the affect and belief work back to the
pragmatic-transport line. The works it cited are registered unread in the
curation entry of 2026-10-24. No experiment was run; every proposed study
is filed as proposed.

**Shape.** Twenty owner turns in three movements. U28 asked for PR [#330](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/330)'s
material to be tied in, and U29–U31 drew on it for tools, revisions and
simulation designs. U33 and U34 brought two of the owner's own ideas: three

a common representation, is the owner's third statement of it ([CLAIM-285](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md),
[TERM-053](../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)); and the hypothesis that two interpretations should give drift
diffusion, the second statement of [CLAIM-262](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md). U35–U36 turned that
hypothesis into a reduction. Then eleven turns, eight of them go-aheads
("get to work", "continue", "proceed", "close the loop"), built a
population lab from v0.2 to v1.0. Three gave direction: U39 (make the
operators learnable), U41 ("take a beat and evaluate") and U45 ("integrate
stable diffusion"), the owner's own U33 option. The replies' recurring
strength was honest scoping of their results: A40, A41 and A44 kept their
null results (3/10, 3/10, 4/8), and A47 kept a baseline that beat its own

what the record holds: the owner's hypothesis ([CLAIM-262](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md)), the exact

## Review of 2026-10-26: the owner's proposals on PerspectiveLab v2.7–v2.9, checked against the lab's stored results and filed as six dated notes

*2026-10-26 04:41:49*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-427 CLAIM-278 CLAIM-336 CLAIM-437 CLAIM-286 — Proposed; entries the proposals named, cited as open -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: QUESTION-088 QUESTION-270 QUESTION-273 QUESTION-031 — Open; questions the proposals named -->

*The owner supplied the lab's v2.7 to v2.9, now in dmarx/PerspectiveLab at
@c54617e: trained affect (v2.7, experiments/trained_affect/), the
perspective engine (v2.8, experiments/perspective_engine/) and endogenous
frames (v2.9, experiments/endogenous_frames/), with reports, handoffs,
architecture specs and three record proposals. The proposals named
eleven entries. They were treated as claims to check, not as
instructions.*

**How it was checked.** Every number kept was read against the stored
results (results/*.csv and *.json) and the code that made them. The test
suites passed: 11 tests for v2.7, 14 for v2.8 and 17 for v2.9. All three
studies were regenerated into a scratch directory, with matplotlib
installed for the run. v2.7 and v2.9 reproduced their stored results byte
for byte. v2.8 reproduced every CSV byte for byte, and its DDM-control
JSON differs only in the last digit of some floats. The notes of
2026-10-26 from PR [#332](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/332) were read first, so as not to repeat them. Where
an entry already had a note of that date, the new one is titled "(later)",
the record's precedent for a second note on one day.

**The notes.** Six were applied, each with a version bump and a history
item.

- [QUESTION-270](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-270.md) (later): v2.7's fitted predictors. Its numbers agree. Two
  facts the proposal left out were added. All eight worlds are one
  logistic law of pursuit with different coefficients, the uptake term
  among them in every world (−0.20 to −1.9). Registration and authority
  are set by the experimenter and given to every predictor as inputs, so
  the question's second requirement, registration measured separately,
  is not met.
- [CLAIM-427](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md) (later): v2.7 to v2.9. The v2.9 proposal called the 15-feature
  ridge regression "an additional stronger conventional comparator". It
  is weaker. It is worse than the selected frame in the five worlds whose
  law does not change, and better only before new feedback in the two
  whose law changes, where both are worse than a constant forecast. Both
  same-feature ties are identities: v2.7's parity row is a copy of the
  fitted uptake predictor, and v2.9's conventional row runs the same
  selection code. On the v2.7 source data a BIC-like score already favours
  the main-effects model before the report's 12-bit surcharge, which the
  proposal did not say.
- [CLAIM-278](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) (later): v2.7 to v2.9. The v2.7 proposal said a conventional
  predictor learns the effect of authority "without representing that
  effect". Its 15-coefficient predictor contains the same three-way
  product of liking, authority and registration, without the sign
  restriction. The sharper fact, used in the note, is that a
  7-coefficient model with main effects and no interaction also beats the
  uptake predictor in the governance world (0.01378 against 0.01586).
- [CLAIM-336](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) (later): frames in the lab. The proposal's statement holds:
  the frame changes what the retained evidence means while the raw
  evidence and the first four updates stay the same, as a lab test checks.
  Two facts were added. Every v2.8 arm except all three changes in the
  85% world scores worse than a constant forecast of one half. And the
  study has no arm with the frame and the raised grant alone, so how
  meaning and influence interact is not isolated. In the 85% world the
  revised operators alone (−0.082 against baseline) do better than the
  frame alone (−0.066).
- [QUESTION-088](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-088.md) (later): v2.7's fitted habit and cue predictors win where
  their phenomenon dominates, within one phenomenon. v2.8 and v2.9 build
  reframing and predict no phenomenon. The proposals' lists of what the
  lab does not yet explain were not copied.
- [QUESTION-273](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-273.md): v2.8 builds one mechanism, a convex share of one step,
  and a sequential mode that only the tests run. Its influence measure
  was corrected in two ways. The report's "matched positive-cue initial
  state" is 16 positive and 8 negative cues, each run started with its arm
  already applied. And the rise of the reframer's exclusion effect from
  0.059 to 0.748 is mostly the new concept, which only the reframer
  writes: excluding it removes that coordinate. A rerun of the lab's code
  on the decision coordinate alone gave 0.247 and 0.069 for the positive
  and negative cue. The note says that the apps its body calls not held
  are now held.

Two descriptions in the v2.9 results were left out of every note and are
recorded here. The critic changes the outcome only in the null world.
There the guarded and unguarded policies differ, and the guarded one
still does worse than admitting nothing (0.25030 against 0.25). Its null
admission rate was 9.375% against a 5% target, as the report says.

**Declined.**

- [CLAIM-437](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md). Its note of 2026-10-26 already says the lab's wanting and
  liking are terms in one logit, with no pursuit or consummatory process.
  v2.7's wanting proxy is anticipated value plus cue drive, so that note
  still holds as written. The proposal's "multiple specified dynamics"
  restates v2.6.
- [CLAIM-286](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md). Its test is [QUESTION-088](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-088.md)'s, as the claim itself says. The
  note on [QUESTION-088](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-088.md) holds v2.7's comparison, and the rest of the
  proposals' points would record only what the lab has not done.
- [CLAIM-453](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-453.md) and [CASE-160](../../record/cases.d/CASE-160.md). v2.8's ddm.py re-checks the linear closure that
  both entries record as checked when filed. The proposal said nonlinear
  workspace transformations "do not inherit it". The lab tests only net
  linear reinforcement (coupling 0.85 or 0.8 against leak 0.6 or 0.5),
  and no nonlinear case is run. Its "exact decomposition" of a changing
  readout into accumulation and reallocation is a three-term algebraic
  identity, the discrete form of [CASE-160](../../record/cases.d/CASE-160.md)'s (dℓ)ᵀx bullet.
- [QUESTION-031](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md). In v2.9 the raw fields and labels are the same for every
  learner. What a unary-only learner fails to separate, a product rule
  against a null world, is a limit of its hypothesis class, not of a
  probe family, and that unary features cannot fit a parity rule is
  textbook. The rest, spurious admission under null cues and grammar
  options outside the search, is in kind what the question's note of
  2026-10-26 already says of v2.5's alarms, or else an absence.
- The v2.9 part of [QUESTION-273](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-273.md)'s proposal. In v2.9 the grant is 0 or 1
  by the critic's verdict, so the separation of capability, evidence
  access and governance is architectural and not measured. The proposal
  itself says it is not the comparison the question asks for.
- The proposals' calls to keep statuses. A note changes none.

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-26, at the owner's request ("the PerspectiveLab
experiments have resulted in some useful discussion we should document on
the nucleation record"), from an exchange titled "Experimental
Infrastructure Review". The share link the owner gave
(https://chatgpt.com/share/6adfa6e4-a0b0-83e9-b3a0-0b53e6000277) could not
be fetched. The owner then uploaded a saved copy of the page ("this should
cover most of it"). The page was virtualized and holds only turns T18 to
T24, numbered as the page numbers them. T0–T17 are absent. They appear to
be the turns in which the lab's v2.x bundles were built, which the record
already holds through dmarx/PerspectiveLab and the entries of 2026-10-26 at
00:30 and 04:41. T24's reply failed to render on the page ("Message
delivery timed out"), and the owner pasted it. No timestamps survive, so
the turns are undated here. A_n is the reply to T_n. T20 reports building
and running "PerspectiveLab v2.11 — Northstar", and offers its bundle for
download. The page carries no files. dmarx/PerspectiveLab holds nothing
past v2.9 (latest import c54617e), and no v2.9.1, v2.10 or v2.11, so every
v2.11 number below is reported, not reproduced. Codes filed from the
exchange carry tmp codes until merge.*

**Shape.** Seven owner turns in two movements. T18 brought the owner's own
idea, employees as "pre-perspectives" that reorganize into the
perspectives driving the organization, and two go-aheads (T19 "flesh this
out further", T20 "make it so") turned it into a design and a reported
build. T21 and T22 brought two more of the owner's ideas, hLDA and the
Indian buffet process, as ways to infer those perspectives rather than
insert them; T23 asked for the generative model to be fleshed out. T24
asked whether the whole setup could serve as an interpretive framework for
how transformers learn. The replies' recurring strength was the one
A40–A47 showed on 2026-10-25: honest scoping. A20 kept a conventional
router that tied its mechanism exactly and called its modes "candidate
organizational modes, not evidence"; A22 and A23 warned that recovering an
IBP from IBP-generated employees shows only "that inference works under
matched assumptions". Their recurring weakness was also the same: they
re-derived what the record holds and cited little of it. A18 and A19 cited
six codes, A20–A23 none, and A24 four. What they re-derived, uncited,
includes [CLAIM-418](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md), [QUESTION-259](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-259.md), [CLAIM-349](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md), [CLAIM-414](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md), [CLAIM-427](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md),
[TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md)'s matched departments, [CASE-101](../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md) and [QUESTION-063](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-063.md) on common
causes, [CASE-158](../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md)'s third prediction and, for T24, [CASE-113](../../record/cases.d/CASE-113.md) and [CLAIM-366](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md).
The mathematics was mostly right; where it was not, the error was at the
size the reply itself chose ([CASE-165](../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md)).

- **T18: "(we should probably also model teams of employees. so maybe
  employees are "pre-perspectives" or sub-perspectives, which can
  reorganize amongst themselves to form the perspectives that influence
  the higher level organizational behavior"**. The owner's idea, and the
  organizational form of [QUESTION-259](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-259.md). A18 accepted it and qualified the
  word: employees "can be full individual interpreters. They're
  constituents of candidate higher-level organizational perspectives". It
  set out a non-tree hierarchy (employees, formal teams, working teams,
  "interpretive coalitions", emergent perspectives, collective behaviour),
  made participation non-exclusive, made teams hyperedges with their own
  state, and inferred perspectives from activity instead of inserting them.
  It ended with Northstar Incident Response as a first experiment.
  **Right:** "a dynamical mode is not automatically a perspective. A
  high-variance activity pattern might merely reflect a shared reporting
  schedule"; "Counting both would inflate the apparent influence of
  coordinated employees"; "Reproducing coalition formation,
  specialization, or groupthink is not by itself a novel result".
  **Missed:** it cited [CASE-134](../../record/cases.d/CASE-134.md) as where Northstar was "already
  considered"; Northstar is [CASE-023](../../record/cases.d/CASE-023.md), and [CASE-134](../../record/cases.d/CASE-134.md) its handoff variant. It

lawful copies (curation entry of 2026-10-26 at 19:45). All thirteen are
Active, with thirteen NOTEs and twenty-two THEORYs, fifteen of them
Active and seven Proposed. They bore out the replies' scoping and
corrected two of their citations: the IBP review gives αH_N only in the
limit, so A23's figure at sixteen features has no source there

into [CASE-165](../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md), [QUESTION-276](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-276.md), [QUESTION-275](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-275.md) and

*2026-10-27 01:01:26*

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-27, at the owner's request ("update the record
to account for this discussion"), from a shared exchange titled "About
the Chagossians" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6adff1a6-6e28-83e8-9796-6439b260b9bb).
It ran from 2026-10-26, 21:18, to 23:04 UTC: twelve owner turns, U1 to
U12, with A_n the reply to U_n (a placeholder turn reporting that custom
instructions were unavailable is not counted). The page served by the
share link carried the conversation only in its embedded data, which was
decoded for this entry; a plain fetch of the page showed only its title.
Each reply was streamed in parts, and the longest copy, which contains
the others, is canonical. The replies read the repository through a
plugin whose output the share redacts, so what they looked at is known
only from what they cite. Their factual particulars about 2025–2026 events
came from searches the share cites by opaque reference; none was checked
here unless a filed entry says so, and several (court rulings of August
and September 2026, news of October 2026) fall after what this filing can
verify. Codes filed from it carry tmp codes until merge.*

**Shape.** Twelve turns in three movements. U1–U3 took the owner's first
case, the Chagossians, from history into the record's lines. U4–U8 added
four more of the owner's cases (federal science and education, USIP, the
police at USIP, the East Wing and CECOT) and drew from them one mechanism,
that an intervention can change what it would take to correct it, and a
reading list. U9–U12 worked the mechanism into a question about correction
between institutions, tied it to the record's ambulance case, and turned to
definitions: the TERM the owner asked for, three more, and a kind for TERMs.
Nine of the twelve owner turns brought a case or a direction of the
owner's own; the replies' recurring strength was keeping what a case can
show apart from what it cannot (every case proposal came with defeaters,
and A6, A7 and A9 each declined to infer intent), and they cited the
record's codes accurately throughout, more than in earlier exchanges. Their
recurring weakness was the one before: they re-derived what the record
holds under new names. A3's central question is [QUESTION-257](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-257.md) almost
verbatim, uncited; the question A9 proposed refines [QUESTION-041](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-041.md), uncited;
A4's claim candidate is [CASE-111](../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md)'s own third consequence; and four of the
replies' names ("remedial reach", "effective remedial capacity", "effective
institutional answerability", "correctability frontier") are one object.

## Audit of 2026-10-27: propositions the record's cases state that no claim holds; eight filed as claims, twenty-four left as candidates

*2026-10-27 02:03:26*

*At the owner's request: "file the claim with a connection to [CASE-111](../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md),
then investigate if other CASEs are potentially hiding CLAIMs we should
expose more explicitly like this." The first filing of the exchange "About
the Chagossians" (workbench entry of 01:01:26) had declined A4's claim
candidate, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational
restoration", because [CASE-111](../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it as a consequence
("Restoration can cost more than preservation"). The owner's point is that
a proposition held only in a case cannot be cited, objected to or given a
status. It is now [CLAIM-463](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md), Active and demonstrated, grounded in
[CASE-111](../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) and illustrated by the federal science, USIP and Chagos cases.*

**Method.** All 171 cases were read in three passes by kind:
constructions (35), specimens (56), and thought experiments with
reported, executed and proposed studies (80). Superseded and Deferred
cases were skipped. For each case, every general proposition it asserts or
derives (usually a bold-lead bullet under "What it shows") was checked
against the titles and claim sections of the claims it links to, and the
titles of all claims were grepped for its key terms. A proposition counted
as held only if some claim's title or claim section says it; a dated note
on a claim does not hold it, which is the second pattern below. Three
read-only agents made the passes; every candidate filed here was then
checked against the case text and the linked claims before filing.

**Filed**, each grounded in its case:

| claim | from | warrant | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-463](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) | [CASE-111](../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md): restoring conditions need not restore a capacity | demonstrated | Active |

The demonstrated claims grounded in Active constructions are Active; those
grounded in the lab's Proposed executed studies ([CASE-161](../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md), [CASE-162](../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md)) stay
Proposed with their cases. One correction in filing: the candidate from

cyclic, incommensurable, captured or" bandit-fed; [CASE-162](../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md)'s reproduced
table has the router ahead on mean error under selective and captured
audits as well, so the claim states the full-information bound and says
the regimes where governance might win are untested or, so far, lost.

**Two patterns.**

- **The lab's findings went into notes.** The strongest candidates from
  studies ([CASE-158](../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md), [CASE-161](../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md), [CASE-162](../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md), [CASE-163](../../record/cases.d/CASE-163.md)) are PerspectiveLab runs
  whose results were filed as dated notes on objection or method claims
  ([CLAIM-278](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md), [CLAIM-414](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md)), so the findings themselves had no codes.
- **Objections waiting for codes.** Five propositions sit in a claim's
  dated note rather than in a claim of their own. On a second reading,
  requested by the owner, two are objections: [CASE-063](../../record/cases.d/CASE-063.md)'s against [CLAIM-212](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md)
  (a narrowing "proposed, not made") and [CASE-067](../../record/cases.d/CASE-067.md)'s against [CLAIM-240](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) ("a
  limit of the model"). A sweep of all claims' notes for the same wording
  found a third, the difficulty [CLAIM-440](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)'s clause 3 records against itself
  from Hesp et al. and Carver. The three are filed as counters,
  [CLAIM-461](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-461.md), [CLAIM-458](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-458.md) and [CLAIM-468](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-468.md), all Proposed. The
  other three notes are not objections, and the first version of this
  entry was wrong to list them as such: [CLAIM-364](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-364.md)'s note lists [CASE-128](../../record/cases.d/CASE-128.md)
  among cases that "add to the claim"; [CLAIM-327](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md)'s says arm B "does not cut
  against it"; [CLAIM-401](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md)'s says "The claim is unchanged". They stay
  candidates for complementary claims, listed below. [CLAIM-096](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-096.md)'s note
  declines a counter on purpose ("It is not filed as a counter: the owner
  did not take the fourth paper up") and is left as it is.

**A tension, not a gap.** [CASE-054](../../record/cases.d/CASE-054.md) (Crow and Hidatsa joking relationships)
says that kind-sharing by descent of an institution "is not a transport of
any token, so it shows that descent and transport are also different
facts". [CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md)'s body says "Descent is supplied by the transport
clause". One of the two needs revising.

Resolved the same day at the owner's word. The two used "descent" for
different relations: [CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md)'s sentence meant a rendering's provenance,
which the transport clause does supply, and [CASE-054](../../record/cases.d/CASE-054.md) meant common
ancestry, in which neither sibling is a rendering of the other.
[CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md)'s sentence now says "provenance", and its third relation names
descent by common ancestry with no transport between the related pair.
[CASE-054](../../record/cases.d/CASE-054.md) now says there is no transport between Crow and Hidatsa, and
leaves open whether each line is a chain of transmissions from the parent
tribe, in which case each branch could have a fidelity relative to the
ancestor. Both are at version 2; neither changes what it claims.

**Left for the owner**, candidates not filed, strongest first in each
group, with the audit's confidence that no claim holds them.

**Threshold.** Rejected near-misses included propositions a linked claim
states (most cases), facts of the case rather than general lessons,
predictions the case hedges ("might", "suggests"), and results from works

candidate, and the eight filed are those that were stated firmly in the
case, checked, and held nowhere else in the record.

## Session of 2026-10-27, 06:20 to 07:46 (U1–U10): from a field that interacts with nothing to structural realism, Barad's apparatus and agential cut, and Jaksland; then luria as an apparatus, the record's scope made unrestricted, and relata to relations as realizations to constraints

*2026-10-27 08:06:54*

*Reconstructed on 2026-10-27, at the owner's request ("update the record
to account for this discussion"), from a shared exchange titled "Field
Existence Question" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6ae058d9-2550-83e8-8f8a-aa0ffff12d7d).
It ran from 2026-10-27, 06:20, to 07:46 UTC: ten owner turns, U1 to U10,
with A_n the reply to U_n (a placeholder turn reporting that custom
instructions were unavailable is not counted). The page served by the
share link carried the conversation only in its embedded data, which was
decoded for this entry; a plain fetch showed only its title. Each reply
was streamed in parts, and the longest copy, which contains the others,
is canonical. A5 and A7 read this repository and luria's through a plugin
whose output the share redacts, so what they looked at is known only from
what they cite. Codes filed from it carry tmp codes until merge.*

**Shape.** Ten turns in three movements. U1–U4 went from a physics
question to a philosophy: a field that interacts with nothing, the
owner's argument from measurement to structural realism, a map of the
neighbourhood, and Barad. U5–U7 brought the philosophy to the record and
then to luria; at U6 the owner made two moves of their own, removing the
domain limit from the record's relational-constitution claims and
observing that a typed relation is less flexible than its relata, and at
U7 found Barad's apparatus in luria. U8–U10 developed the owner's
analogy, relata to relations as realizations to specifications, with
prior art, and synthesized it. The replies' recurring strength was the
guard the record already keeps: every move past evidence was marked as
interpretation (A1 "a proposed philosophical criterion, not a theorem",
A4 "the mathematical result does not itself establish this ontology", A7
"Demonstrable" against "Philosophical hypothesis", A10's three levels). Their
recurring weakness was the earlier exchanges': they did not find what the
record holds outside the codes they were shown. A7's reflexive apparatus
is [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md), filed five days before; A9 named Montévil and Mossio,
Pattee, Ladyman and Lorenzetti, Brandom and Searle as prior art to read,
all read here, with no code; and A4's closing proposal is [CLAIM-405](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md).

- **U1 (06:20): "can a field meaningfully exist if it doesn't interact
  with anything?"** A1 separated existence from physically meaningful
  existence, by counterfactual distinguishability. **Right:** the
  conclusion "establishes that **its existence makes no empirically
  accessible difference**", not that it does not exist; "absence of direct
  coupling is not equivalent to absence of all physically significant
  relations" (a free field has energy–momentum, and gravitates); and the
  question it ended on, "Is interaction merely how we discover that
  something exists, or is interaction … part of what it means for
  something to exist in the first place?" **Filed:** nothing on its own;
  its second half is [QUESTION-284](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-284.md). **Not filed:** A1's criterion, ∃F
  meaningfully ⟹ ∃ΔR(F), which it called a proposal.
- **U2 (06:23): "all of our access to the world is mediated by
  measurements and measuring instruments. measurements are necessarily
  interactions. interactions definitionally involve multiple parties.
  something something structural realism."** A2 laid the owner's argument
  out in five steps and marked the fifth, that physical existence just is
  participation in relational structure, as the leap from epistemic to
  ontic structural realism. **Right:** "We can know only relations ⇏ Only
  relations exist"; "What makes a purportedly intrinsic feature of reality
  a physical fact if changing it could never change any possible
  interaction?"; the gauge caveat ("gauge equivalence is generally
  supported by more theoretical structure than observational
  indistinguishability alone"). **Missed:** the inference it guards is
  [CLAIM-150](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)'s, and the relata problem it closed on is Chakravartty's
  dilemma ([THEORY-034](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md)), with the record's non-eliminative choice in
  [CLAIM-136](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md); it had not been pointed at the record. **Filed:** nothing new.
  **Not filed:** operational equivalence classes of worlds as the bearers
  of physical ontology, which appeared once.
- **U3 (06:25): "relevant thinkers in the neighborhood of our
  discussion"**. A3 gave Barad, Ladyman and Rovelli as closest; Bohr,
  Poincaré, Cassirer, Peirce and Bridgman as ancestors; Whitehead, Esfeld
  and Wheeler, with Bateson and Dewey; van Fraassen, Newman and
  Chakravartty as critics; and four positions from epistemic relationalism
  to radical relational ontology. **Right:** "These are conceptual
  positions, not a strict ordering of the named philosophers' entire
  systems"; and its last question, whether existence is constituted by
  actual interactions, possible ones, or "its place in a law-governed
  structure of counterfactual interactions". **Missed:** the record holds
  the Stanford entry it recommended ([LIT-045](../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md), read), Ladyman's 1998 paper
  and *Every Thing Must Go* ([LIT-342](../../record/literature.d/LIT-342.md), [LIT-301](../../record/literature.d/LIT-301.md), both unavailable), Esfeld
  and Lam ([LIT-895](../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), read in [NOTE-695](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-695.md)), Chakravartty ([LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md)), Worrall
  ([LIT-315](../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md)) and Rovelli's later account ([LIT-177](../../record/literature.d/LIT-177.md)); "*A Moderate Structural
  Realism* (2004)" names no work that could be identified, and the
  Esfeld it describes is Esfeld and Lam's. **Filed:** Rovelli 1996,
  Newman 1928 and van Fraassen 1980 registered unread (curation entry of

decoded from the page's embedded data as before. It continues the turns filed
in the workbench entries of 08:06 (U1–U10) and 09:14 (U11–U14). This entry
covers nine owner turns, U15 to U23, 14:41 to 16:19 UTC, with replies to 16:26.

model that can be checked, and the model was used to say where the conjecture
holds and where it fails. A20 to A22 did this for U20 with two-variable
couplings, a Laplacian spectrum, a frustrated cycle and a three-node

Spivak is [LIT-803](../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), Skimmed. A17's entrenchment is [CLAIM-184](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md). Entries filed
earlier the same day were not cited, because they are on this branch and not

## The owner's review of the pull request (2026-10-27, evening): six changes before merging, made the same evening; correspondence generation, memory as constraint, the higher-order reduction, the luria split, rates against time scales, and a synthesis

*2026-10-27 18:25:54*

The owner reviewed the pull request that filed the exchange "Field Existence
Question" and its readings. The verdict was "revise, then merge". It praised
the PR because "the formal results force the ontology to become more precise"
and because it keeps negative findings ("I would not soften the counterexample
to keep the original proposition alive"). Each change it asked for was made:

- **Generating a correspondence against discovering one.** [CLAIM-471](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md) is
  restated, version 2, around three mechanisms:
  - physical constraint formation;
  - correspondence discovery;
  - correspondence adaptation.

  Only the first bears on the strong thesis. The readings had found the
  correspondence maps given in nearly every formalism. [QUESTION-282](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md) asks
  when interaction changes the operative correspondence structure. It also
  covers the review's sixth point, that "the spectral mathematics ordinarily
  assumes the operator has already been specified".
- **Memory is a constraint.** [CLAIM-480](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md), version 2. A history-dependent
  boundary relation constrains admissible trajectories, and separation of
  time scales decides only whether the constraint is approximately
  memoryless. [CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s note that had said otherwise is corrected.
- **The higher-order reduction promoted.** Hansen and Ghrist's v₁ = v₂ + v₃
  ([THEORY-1090](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md)) is now in [CLAIM-480](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)'s title and body, and the
  claim is grounded in it. [QUESTION-283](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md) asks when composition forces a
  richer relational vocabulary. The review called it the result "I'd most
  want to preserve".
- **The luria claim split.** [CLAIM-469](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md) is the operational claim,
  without Barad, in [TERM-089](../../record/terms.d/TERM-089.md)'s sense, which is adopted.
  [CLAIM-476](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md), version 2, keeps the constitutive thesis and rests on it.
- **Rates are not time scales.** Both rate studies, [CASE-180](../../record/cases.d/CASE-180.md) and
  [CASE-178](../../record/cases.d/CASE-178.md), now separate three readings:
  - different event rates, which is demonstrated;
  - separate operating regimes, which is plausible;
  - a dynamically generated hierarchy, which is an interpretation.
- **A synthesis.** [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) lists five relationships and where each
  implication fails. [CASE-179](../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md) is the proposed study in which coupling,
  correspondence maps and apparatus revision are varied independently.

Two pre-merge checks the review raised were answered without change.
- **The changelog's `record/...` links are correct.** Fragments in
  `record/changelog.d/` are collected into the root `CHANGELOG.md`
  (`fragments:` in luria.yaml), and main's CHANGELOG already links that way.
- **The Docs runs reported `action_required`** were on the bot's
  repair commits. GitHub holds runs triggered by the bot for approval. The
  last run on an authored commit had passed, and the held run was re-run by
  the owner.

The review's own judgments are recorded here and not filed as claims. Its
reasons are in the entries it changed.

that the same loop entrenches whatever gained influence early. The record
had stated both loops and constructed neither. [CASE-182](../../record/cases.d/CASE-182.md) builds them
under one endorsement rule (scratch/formal/trust_loop.py, 200 seeds).

- **Scored every round:** the more accurate operator ends ahead in
  200/200 seeds, even after a head start for the other.
- **Scored only when acting, under sharp selection (β ≥ 30):** the early
  leader is never displaced, 200/200.
- **Soft selection (β = 8):** the better operator recovers, after a median
  of 460 rounds.

The first run printed "True" for a check it never made. The line was a
literal, and it was caught on reading and replaced by the measurement. The
first run also showed no entrenchment at β = 8. That is a finding and not a
failure: entrenchment needs selection sharp enough that the stale estimate
is never revisited. The body said [CLAIM-277](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md) rests on [CLAIM-282](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md), which is

- **Reading-THEORYs.** THEORYs filed from a single reading almost never

- **Wide-form THEORYs.** THEORYs filed by [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4's narrowing sweep,

## What accepting ADR-061 would change: of 65 claims classified as about support or a source, 30 move on a close reading, into 28 new ARGs

*2026-10-28 05:19:34*

**What this is.** A preview, filed with [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md) while it is Proposed, of
the migration its acceptance would trigger. Nothing here is applied. On
2026-10-28 four reviewers read every claim the decision's classification
names (65 of them), on main after the fifth status review, and said for
each what the migration would do. Each call names the ARG it would file:
premises, conclusion, form and status, and the critical question that
carries the verdict. The calls were checked against each other, and where
two moves interact the interaction is said below.

**The headline: the classifier overcounted by half.** Of 65 claims, 35
stay claims on a close reading, 18 split, 10 become ARGs outright and 2
fold into a THEORY's reading plus a Rejected ARG. The low-confidence calls
shrank as the decision expected, and so did some high ones. Most claims
that stay are `disclaimed` boundary claims of the form "X does not
establish Y" where X is not an entry in the record, so there is no
inference between entries to file; [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) already called them claims the
record disowns. The rest that stay are about the subject matter after all,
or are about whether a defeat condition can be met, which the decision
already keeps.

| | Count |
|---|---|
| New ARGs | 28 (29 calls; [CLAIM-053](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-053.md)'s and [CLAIM-229](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md)'s first ARG are one inference) |
| of which Rejected / Proposed / Active | 15 / 12 / 1 |
| Existing ARGs revised (a critical-question answer added) | 3: [ARG-003](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-003.md), [ARG-006](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md), [ARG-008](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-008.md) |
| Claims Superseded | 12 |
| Claims revised (a split, a trim, or new edges) | 19 |
| Claims unchanged | 35 |
| THEORY revisions | 0 required; [THEORY-168](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) may gain a line |
| New CASEs needed as premises | 2 |
| Field edges repointed | about 60, and about 15 more become body text |

The forms used: `evidence` most often, then `analogy`, `formal-application`,
`existence`, `abduction` and `source`. Both new forms are used, `source` by
three ARGs.

**Three worked examples.**

*An objection to an inference becomes the inference, Proposed: [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md).*
Now a counter that `objects_to` [CLAIM-162](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) and grounds on [THEORY-069](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md).
After, one file:

    # new ARG: form analogy, status Proposed
    rests_on: [CLAIM-169](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md)
    grounds: [[THEORY-069](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md), [THEORY-070](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md)]
    concludes: [CLAIM-162](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md)
    # body: "what relevant difference is there?" is answered: "Interests
    # whose curves do not cross are not coupled, have no phase, and do not
    # 'lock'". [CLAIM-198](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md), which supplies the missing coupling, enters a
    # later version as a premise.

[CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) goes Superseded by it. Its one inbound objection, [CLAIM-198](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md),
cannot `objects_to` an ARG, so it becomes a premise of the ARG's next
version, as the decision's "one ARG per inference" says.

*A source claim becomes a THEORY's reading plus a Rejected ARG:
[CLAIM-072](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-072.md).* Now a granted claim that Saussure says "purely differential"
only of signifier and signified taken apart. [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md) already holds all
of that, so it gains nothing. What [CLAIM-072](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-072.md) adds is a verdict on
support, and it holds two inferences, not one:

    # ARG A: form source, status Rejected
    grounds: [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md)
    concludes: [CLAIM-082](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)      # "drop the referent contrast, which is not Saussure's"
    # ARG B: form source, status Proposed
    rests_on: [CLAIM-082](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)
    grounds: [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md)
    concludes: [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)      # [CLAIM-254](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md)'s objection is a revision of this one

[CLAIM-072](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-072.md) goes Superseded by both, and [CLAIM-254](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md) too.

*A claim others rest on is split, and the verdict goes to an ARG that
exists: [CLAIM-085](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md).* Now granted and Active, and [CLAIM-243](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-248](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-248.md) and
[CLAIM-252](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md) rest on it. Its circularity limb, "That would primarily

which already names it. So [ARG-008](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-008.md) gains that answer in version 2 and stays
Active, and [CLAIM-085](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md) is retitled to its subject-matter part: "A framing
effect in a language model is a property of that model under those
prompts, and what a translation ought to preserve is a normative question
that model response distributions, being descriptive, cannot settle." Its
three dependents keep `rests_on`; nothing is repointed.

**What the preview found wrong in the decision, now corrected in it.**

- *[CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md)'s example named the wrong premise.* The analogy's source is
  [THEORY-069](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md), phase synchrony, which [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) grounds on. [THEORY-070](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) is
  [CLAIM-162](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md)'s own premise.
- *The split rule must be applied after the moves, not before.* [CLAIM-053](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-053.md)
  is forced to split only because Active [CLAIM-229](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md) rests on it, and
  [CLAIM-229](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md) itself becomes ARGs; the same holds for [CLAIM-066](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-066.md) and
  [CLAIM-234](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-234.md). A move that removes a claim's last Active dependent frees the
  claim to move too, and two moves that file the same inference file it
  once.
- *[CLAIM-066](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-066.md) belongs on the forced-split list*, and [CLAIM-011](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md) does not: its
  title holds no support clause, and the verdict is already [ARG-006](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md)'s.
- *[CLAIM-097](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-097.md) has a THEORY behind it*, [THEORY-522](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-522.md), which reads
  T2I-CompBench. It stays a claim and gains that ground.
- *[CLAIM-169](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) is not a SOURCE case.* The decision uses it as a claim
  premise, and it stays one.
- *Five "what a test could show" claims are about defeat conditions*
  ([CLAIM-206](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), -208, -222, -226, -244), the group the decision keeps.
- *[CLAIM-073](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-073.md)*, a Rejected support claim, is missing from the
  classification.
- *The ARG scheme lacks slots a moved claim uses.* ARG has `rests_on`,
  `grounds`, `concludes`, `undercut_by` and `superseded_by`. A claim moved
  to an ARG loses `works` ([CLAIM-427](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md) is in a manuscript), `defeated_if`,
  `uses`, `complements` and `illustrated_by`. Either the scheme gains
  `uses` and `works`, or those go to the body. And `objects_to` cannot
  target an ARG, so a reply to a moved objection becomes a premise of the
  ARG's next version.
- *Two moves need a CASE that does not exist yet*: the anchoring measures
  behind [CLAIM-190](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md), and the central defeat test behind [CLAIM-232](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md) and
  [CLAIM-233](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md).

**What the record would notice.** The 30 moving claims are cited in 442
files, and the 12 that would be Superseded in 175, mostly in prose and
acknowledgement directives. The repair rewrites links mechanically; what
a citation should now say is read entry by entry. The lint's checks would see
three things change.
- Superseded claims cited as open lose their `inactive-ok` reason, which

- No Active claim would rest on a retired one, because of the split rule.
- The dialectic page would gain each new ARG once the pin moves to luria

## The twelfth status review: four terms adopted, three formal readings proved, two splits, and ARG-022 rejected on its own condition

*2026-10-29 10:17:26*

**What the pass took.** Pass 11 left the worklist with no inversions, no
unwritten concessions, no retired premises and no answered-but-open
questions, so this pass worked the load-bearing Proposed readings and the
claims they hold. It ran five clusters: [CLAIM-115](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s translation successors,
four Proposed TERMs, the formal readings ([THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md), -156, -167, -168), the
agency and self readings ([THEORY-214](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md), -219, -220, -628, -1114), and the social
and cognitive readings ([THEORY-327](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md), -335, -411, -662, -892). Five reviewers
read, the rulings were given here, and each reviewer then applied its own
cluster. Every cluster was checked before it was committed.

**Checks run before anything was applied.** Three of the formal readings
were promoted on re-derivations, and their scripts were re-run here.

- **[THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md) (the real Schur corollary).** One group of each real type
  matches the predicted commutant and symmetric-commutant dimensions: S₃ for
  ℝ (9 and 6), ℤ/5 for ℂ (18 and 9), and Q8 for ℍ (16 and 6). The generic
  multiplicities match too: (2,2,2), (2,2,2) and (4,4).
  - Two controls have simple spectra: a random symmetric matrix, and a
    commuting operator given a 10⁻³ non-commuting perturbation.
  - The 3-cube Laplacian commutes with both B₃ and S₃, and its two middle
    levels are irreducible under the first and reducible under the second.
    So one spectrum fits two groups, which is [CLAIM-385](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-385.md)'s point.
- **[THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) (Blackwell's converse).** The garbling identities hold to
  3×10⁻¹⁵. The convex-order splitting residual falls from 8.3×10⁻³ to
  1.1×10⁻³ as the iteration count grows. A control pair that is not in convex
  order stays at 5.5×10⁻².
- **[THEORY-168](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) (Theorem 4.6 and CbD 1.0).** A brute-force check by max flow
  agrees with nominal dominance on every random pair at k = 3, 4 and 5. The
  worked non-heredity case reproduces:
  - Pr[V₂≠V₃] is forced to 0.52, where a maximal coupling needs 0.20.
  - The case is noncontextual under 1.0, contextual under 2.0, and its
    subsystem is contextual under 1.0.

  The reviewer's side finding was checked by hand. For a binary content in
  three contexts, maximizing Pr[all equal] fixes Pr[all 1] = p₁ and
  Pr[all 0] = 1 − p₃, and then p₂ fixes the last two patterns. So the maximal
  coupling is unique, and binary connections first separate 1.0 from 2.0 at
  four contexts. The summary now says so.

  - The Fisher information of the source minus the target's has no
