## The fifteenth status review: nine claims and three readings promoted, two terms adopted, and ADR-047's kind-1 rule restored

*2026-10-30 00:34:57*

**What the pass took.** The worklist on main after pass 14 had nothing in
its problem sections, and the reliance ranking is now flat: almost every
Proposed entry has one dependent. The pass took five clusters:

- what pass 14 left;
- the Proposed terms;
- the consciousness readings;
- the social and evolutionary readings;
- the formal and philosophical readings.

Five reviewers read and the rulings were given here. Each reviewer then
applied its own cluster, and each cluster was checked before commit.

**A finding about earlier passes.** Reviewer C pointed out that [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s "Where a
narrowing's dropped claims go", one of the evidence rulings [ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps,
sorts each clause a narrowing drops into four kinds:

- **Kind 1, a generalization the source asserts.** It becomes a Proposed
  THEORY that keeps the wide wording, `extends` the narrowed entry and
  inherits the old promote_when.
- **Kind 2, the record's own gloss.** It becomes an interpretive CLAIM.
- **Kind 3, a mis-statement.** It gets a note only.
- **Kind 4, open scope nobody asserts.** It becomes a QUESTION.

From pass 8 on, the review's rulings narrowed readings and moved the
promote_when to a new QUESTION every time. Where the source asserts the wide
form, that dropped it. The fault is in the rulings given here, not in the
reviewers' work: the briefs cited [THEORY-285](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) → [QUESTION-303](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md) as the pattern,
and nobody checked it against the later section of [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md).

Twenty-eight QUESTIONs on main hold a promote_when moved this way. They
cover about thirty readings, from [THEORY-285](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) (pass 8) to [THEORY-140](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md)
(pass 14). Some are genuinely kind 4. The others need a kind-1 entry. That
sweep is its own branch, after this pass.

**This pass follows the rule.**

- **[THEORY-164](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md)** is narrowed to what Raviv, Meyer and Lev-Ari report. Its wide
  form, which the paper asserts, is kept as a Proposed reading that extends
  it and inherits the promote_when.
- **[THEORY-174](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)** is promoted on a checked re-derivation of Theorem 44. The
  adaptive analogue, which [LIT-845](../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md) §6.2 asserts without proof, is kept as a
  Proposed reading (kind 1). The narrowing to no-signalling models, and to
  hom models satisfying the predicate, corrects an imprecise statement
  (kind 3).
- **[THEORY-034](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md)** is narrowed to the seven texts its census places. The
  founding texts nobody has placed are open scope (kind 4), so that part is a
  QUESTION.
- **Readings not narrowed.** Narrowing would free nothing, and a kind-1 entry
  would add a Proposed entry for no gain, so these readings stay Proposed:
  - [THEORY-135](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-135.md), -141, -137, -143, -151, -025, -036 and -170;
  - [THEORY-090](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md), which was proposed for a split.

  Their edges to the claims they only corroborate moved to `corroborated_by`
  ([ADR-058](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)). That is what frees the claims. Pass 12's rule decides it: split
  or narrow only where it frees a dependent, or where the reading is
  promotable on its own.

**Checks run before anything was applied.** The formal cluster's two scripts
were re-run here.

- **Theorem 44** ([THEORY-174](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)), on the binary triangle as both scenarios:
  52,472 deterministic procedures and 12,152 distinct maps.
  - The direct semantics and the hom-scenario semantics agree exactly on 20
    random procedures × 10 no-signalling models, the strongly contextual one
    included.
  - The linear program recognises random classical maps to 10⁻¹⁴, and the
    procedure it recovers reproduces the map on contextual models.
  - Two contextual hom models with non-classical maps are rejected (residual
    1.63).
  - A contextual hom model that induces a classical map is accepted. So
    e ↦ F_e is not injective, and the theorem's "some" matters.
  - A signalling source makes the result depend on the choice of context
    (0.50), which shows the check can see it.
- **[THEORY-186](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s random-start claim.** From small random starts, the
  off-diagonal part of the product falls from 15% to 2% of the largest
  strength as the scale falls from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁴. A decoupled start gives the
  exact solution, and the shallow control shows no ordering. This agrees
  with the reading, but its promote_when asks for a proof and rules out
  simulation, so it stays Proposed.

rulings, not the reviewers' work. The briefs cited [THEORY-285](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) → [QUESTION-303](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md)
as the pattern, and nobody checked that pattern against [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s later
section, "Where a narrowing's dropped claims go". [ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps that section
among the evidence rulings it carries forward. The section sorts every
dropped clause into one of four kinds:

1. **A generalization the source asserts** becomes a Proposed THEORY. It
   keeps the old wording, extends the narrowed entry, and inherits the old
   promote_when.
2. **The record's own gloss** becomes an interpretive CLAIM.
3. **A mis-statement** gets a dated note.
4. **Open scope nobody asserts**, and only that, becomes a QUESTION.

The fifteenth review found the gap (workbench entry of 2026-10-30, 00:34).

**What the sweep did.** Four agents took the 28 QUESTIONs those passes filed.
Between them the QUESTIONs cover 31 readings from [THEORY-285](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) to [THEORY-140](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md).
For each reading the agent sorted every dropped clause, citing the NOTE in
which the source asserts it or does not.

| Kind | Result |
|---|---|
| 1, wide form the source asserts | 22 new Proposed readings |
| 2, the record's own extrapolation | 2 new interpretive claims |
| 3, mis-statement | 7 dated notes |
| nothing new to file | 6 readings |

- **Kind 1, 22 readings.** Each new reading extends its narrowed Active entry,
  inherits its promote_when, and bears on the QUESTION that held it.
- **Kind 2, 2 claims:**
  - that the barrier left after alignment rises with depth, which no source
    states for aligned barriers;
  - that averaging weights within a basin averages features, which [NOTE-512](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md)
    offers as the record's own candidate.
- **Kind 3, 7 notes, on [THEORY-335](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md), -481, -913, -904, -146, -917 and -920.**
  Examples:
  - [THEORY-904](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md)'s d = .79 is a difference between goal intentions, not a plan
    effect.
  - [THEORY-917](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-917.md)'s old title turned "no study links them" into "no relation".
  - [THEORY-146](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)'s "only if" was a necessity the paper never claims.
- **Nothing new to file, 6 readings:**
  - [THEORY-922](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-922.md), -910, -903, -900 and -912 were not narrowed at all; only
    their promote_when moved, so their QUESTIONs are open scope (kind 4).
  - [THEORY-140](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md)'s one dropped clause was already judged kind 3 at the
    fourteenth review.

**The QUESTIONs stay Open.** [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) rejected filing a dropped clause only as
a QUESTION, "which asks without proposing". It did not forbid a QUESTION
beside the proposal. So each kind-1 reading bears on its QUESTION and nothing
is retired.

**Where the title is not verbatim.** Four of the 22 titles are trimmed or
reworded:

- **Mixed kinds, trimmed.** Where an old title mixed a kind-1 core with a
  kind-2 or kind-3 clause, the new reading carries only the core:
  - from [THEORY-112](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md), the depth clause;
  - from [THEORY-111](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md), the averaging clause;
  - from [THEORY-904](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md), the misread effect size;
  - from [THEORY-917](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-917.md), the null on random exploration.

  Each summary says what was left out. This follows [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md): the routing is
  clause by clause.
- **Reworded:** the reading kept from [THEORY-146](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md) restates "counteracts this
  only if it discounts" as "a funder that discounts counteracts this",
  dropping the necessity.

**Close calls the agents flagged.**

- **[THEORY-214](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md)'s equilibrium of attack and repair:** kind 1, not kind 3. The
  neglect finding ([QUESTION-169](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-169.md)) qualifies the claim rather than

- **Readings that differ from their Active entries mainly in voice:**
  [THEORY-918](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-918.md)'s "reliably improved", [THEORY-908](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md)'s causal verbs, and [THEORY-897](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-897.md)

**The template is fixed.** The review brief now routes dropped clauses by

## The status-review procedure revised after sixteen passes, and a fresh worklist

*2026-10-30 02:44:15*

**Why now.** The owner asked, after the sixteenth pass, to revisit the triage
procedure before the next pass and to build a fresh worklist from the
record's current state. [ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) set the procedure on 2026-10-27. Sixteen
passes and the [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep have run since then.

**What the procedure got wrong, measured on main after pass 16.**

- **The ranking had stopped ranking.** [ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) ordered work by reach: how
  many entries rest, transitively, on a Proposed one. When it was adopted,
  the top entries had 19, 13 and 13 dependents. Now the most any Proposed
  entry has is 1, and only 13 entries have any. From pass 12 on, clusters
  were chosen by hand.
- **The unblocked list read no blocker notes.** 124 claims were listed as
  unblocked, and 45 of them already carried a recent note saying what they
  wait on. A pass had to read each one to find that out.
- **The move that freed most claims had no section.** In passes 13 to 16
  most promotions came from showing that a Proposed ground was corroboration
  ([ADR-058](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)). The worklist showed only the premise, not that it was the one
  thing holding the claim back.
- **The procedure was not in the record.** The reviewer brief, the
  conventions for applying rulings, and a local check for inverted grounds
  lived in a session's scratchpad. That is how the wrong precedent for a
  narrowing's dropped clauses travelled for seven passes before a reviewer
  checked it against [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md). The brief still carried a variant of it
  ("move the rest to a QUESTION") until today.

**What changed.**

- **The worklist's order** ([ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) version 6). The sections that must be
  empty come first. Stale converses joins them: a Proposed reading still
  listing an Active claim under `supports` is an inverted ground waiting for
  the repair bot. Then the work, in the order a pass takes it:
  1. claims ready for a ruling, grouped by line;
  2. sole blockers, the unheld premises ranked by how many claims each alone
     holds back;
  3. blocker notes that a premise has changed since;
  4. unblocked claims held by a recent note;
  5. Proposed readings no source of which is read in full, which need
     reading, not review.

  Reach is printed last.
- **The tests.** Each new section is fired on the fixture record in
  `test_worklist.py`. The suite went from 13 tests to 18.
- **The procedure.** `record/status-review/README.md` now holds it, with the
  narrowing rule as [ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) states it and the conventions every pass applied.
  It also records the owner's delegation of rulings of 2026-10-29.

**What did not change.** The criteria for promotion, the evidence rulings,
and the rule that reasoning lives on the entries.

`written()` still counts any history note that names an objection, even one
that only adds the `objected_by` edge. This is a known limit, left because
tightening it would need the note to say what was conceded, and no field
holds that.

Stale `inactive-ok` acknowledgements are left to the lint, which already
reports them ([DP-004](../design-principles.md#dp-4)).

**The fresh worklist, on main at 46c6cb81a.** The sections that must be
empty are empty.

| Section | Count |
|---|---|
| Ready for a ruling | 79 |
| Sole blockers | 30 premises |
| Held by a recent blocker note | 45 |
| Proposed readings not read in full | 7 |
| Blocker notes a premise has changed since | none |

- **Ready for a ruling, by line.** None of the 79 has been reviewed under
  [ADR-057](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md).

  | Line | Ready |
  |---|---|
  | pragmatic-transport | 32 |
  | distributed-agency | 26 |
  | nucleating-argument | 6 |
  | will-organization | 6 |
  | authenticity | 2 |

  | learned-structure | 2 |
  | organizational-affect | 2 |
  | formal-apparatus | 1 |

- **Sole blockers.** Four premises each alone hold two claims back:
  - [CLAIM-004](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-004.md) ([CLAIM-143](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md), [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md));
  - [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) ([CLAIM-137](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-137.md), [CLAIM-217](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md));
  - [THEORY-1114](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1114.md) ([CLAIM-491](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md), [CLAIM-493](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md));
  - [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md) ([CLAIM-082](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md), [CLAIM-242](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-242.md)).

  The other 26 hold one claim each.
- **Held.** The 45 held claims return as work from 2026-11-10, when the

- **Not read in full.** The 7 readings that need reading are [THEORY-316](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-316.md),

- **[CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s bound was wrong.** Its title said no deterministic rule
  without foresight does better than twice the hindsight optimum. With a
  per-use cost a = c_a + u on the filed state, the break-even rule is within
  2 − a/c_r, and nothing does materially better. So "twice" holds only as
  a/c_r goes to 0. Filing once the overpayment has *reached* the cost of
  filing can exceed 2 (3.55 in the reviewer's search). The reviewer derived
  the bound and checked it numerically in p18/rent_or_buy.py. It was

## The twenty-second status review: ADR-065 applied to 58 readings

*2026-10-30 08:29:54*

**What the pass took.** [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) was filed this morning, in the same pull
request, from a survey of every Proposed THEORY's promote_when. The survey
flagged about 58 whose conditions ask for more than their titles assert.
This pass reviewed those 58 in six clusters: two of one-study titles, one of
attribution titles, the endosymbiosis batch of 2026-10-27, one of titles to
narrow first, and one of proofs waiting on a second checker. Six reviewers
read, the rulings were made here, and the same reviewers applied them.

**53 promoted, 5 kept.**

- **The 53 are now Active.** For each, the reading the title states is
  read in full, and nothing in the record contradicts it.
- **What a promote_when asked beyond the title was kept.** It went to one
  of three places:
  - a Proposed THEORY that `extends` the reading and keeps the old
    condition word for word, where the source asserts the wider thesis
    ([ADR-047](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1);
  - a QUESTION, where it does not;
  - an interpretive CLAIM, where the old title carried the record's own
    critique (kind 2).

  That made 46 new entries: 32 THEORYs, 10 QUESTIONs and 4 CLAIMs.
- **Kept Proposed:**
  - **[THEORY-989](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md)** and **[THEORY-613](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md)**: [THEORY-989](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md)'s condition disputes the
    study's own estimator (§7); [THEORY-613](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md)'s dimension count is
    inconsistent in the copy read, so the version of record is asked for
    (§4).
  - **[THEORY-1192](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1192.md)**, **[THEORY-564](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md)** and **[THEORY-351](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md)**: their titles are
    general (§6). [THEORY-1192](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1192.md)'s condition asked for less than its title
    claims, and now asks for the per-domain bias-corrected estimates.

**The review found errors, not just missing hedges.** The survey's premise
was that these titles were fine and their conditions too strict. For most
that held. But a careful reading for promotion found titles that misstate
their sources:

- **[THEORY-375](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-375.md)**: MRU beat LRU by up to 9.6 times, not 2.3. The 2.3 was
  its margin over the distance value.
- **[THEORY-383](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-383.md)**: "whenever updates arrived" contradicts the authors' own
  conclusion that the stored result won below five updates a second.
- **[THEORY-1158](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1158.md)**: "without beating spectral synchronization" is false
  against plain spectral synchronization, on three of four rows of Table 1.
- **[THEORY-889](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-889.md)**: the thermometer effect is about a third of a standard
  deviation, not a tenth (p. 626).
- **[THEORY-1104](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md)**: "no pathway from one donor" missed the Myxococcota
  lead in two pathways.
- **[THEORY-924](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-924.md)**: Elo ratings are the row means of the log-odds only when
  those have no cyclic component. In the entry's own copy example the
  batch fixed point is ±71.9 Elo points, against row means of ±95.4.
- **[THEORY-943](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-943.md)**: uninformative equilibria exist in the authors'
  two-signal example, not in general. A four-signal model under the
  quadratic rule has none; it is written out in the entry. The recorded
  misreport score of −0.754 is −0.760, and −0.754 comes from rounded
  posteriors.

Each wrong clause is dropped with a dated note (kind 3), or corrected in
the wide form filed beside the reading. A reading's title had gone
unchecked against its source as long as nothing tried to promote it; the
same is likely true of the Proposed readings [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) did not flag.

**The second checker re-derived, and the bodies now carry the work.**
[ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §5 counts a re-derivation recorded in the file once a second
checker has followed it. The original scripts were not on the machine, so
the checker wrote its own, numpy only, each with a control that had to
fail. Scripts in a session's scratchpad are not in the record. So each of
the ten proof entries now writes its derivation out, and says in a
sentence what was run, on how many cases, and what the control did.
Someone can redo it from the file alone.

**Two rules came out of applying the decision.**

- **An `answers` edge is not an attribution.** All twelve endosymbiosis
  readings `answered` [QUESTION-277](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-277.md). Promoting them would have left an Open
  question with Active answers. None answers it as posed, so each is now
  `bears_on` ([ADR-060](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-060.md)).
- **The README and [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) disagreed on the version of record.** §4 drops a
  demand for it where no discrepancy is named. The README sent it to a
  QUESTION. The README is corrected. Five entries dropped the demand:
  [THEORY-899](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md), [THEORY-926](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-926.md) and [THEORY-943](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-943.md), and the wide forms beside
  [THEORY-927](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) and [THEORY-911](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-911.md). The last says that only the abstract was
  compared, so a discrepancy in its counts would restore the demand.

**Closing checks.**

- **The worklist on the branch.** Its six must-be-empty sections are empty.
- **Ready for a ruling.** The four new interpretive CLAIMs are now listed
  as ready. They were filed today and take their ruling next pass.
- **Stale directives.** 47 inactive-ok lines in 46 files named a reading
  promoted here; they are trimmed.
- **Two NOTEs pointed at moved conditions.** [NOTE-1334](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1334.md) and [NOTE-1341](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1341.md) now
  point to where the conditions went.
- **A concretize gap.** [NOTE-1341](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1341.md)'s heading still carried its temporary
  code from concretize, the only file in the record that did; it is
  corrected.

**Left for later.**

- **[THEORY-1100](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1100.md)** has the endosymbiosis batch's attribution shape and was
  outside the survey's list.
- **The survey's flags were keyword estimates.** Readings with this shape
  that it missed will surface as intake applies [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), or at review.

## The twenty-fourth status review: ADR-065 swept by reading

*2026-10-30 18:30:10*

**Why a sweep.** After pass 23 the worklist held nothing to rule on. Its six
must-be-empty sections were empty, no claim was ready, and every sole blocker
and blocker note was covered by a note under 14 days old. The one standing
doubt was [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)'s survey. It found its 58 readings by keyword flags, and it
missed at least [THEORY-871](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md) and [THEORY-1100](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1100.md). So this pass re-checked the record
by reading it.

**Triage.** Five read-only reviewers took the 570 Proposed readings that have
a source read in full. Each worked from a digest of title, condition and
sources, opening the files only when the digest could not decide. They were
told to put a title in the narrow-first class whenever a number or scope word
in it could not be matched to its source. The result:

| Class | What it means | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Report | the condition asks more than the title asserts | 28 |
| Proof | waiting on a second checker | 7 |
| Narrow first | the title must be narrowed before it can be ruled on | 51 |
| General, internal-validity or not promotable | the condition stands | about 484 |

About 160 of the general entries are the wide forms filed beside reported
entries on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30, so they are general by construction.

**Rulings.** Four reviewers took the 35 report and proof entries, and a fifth
took three leftovers: [CLAIM-471](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md), [THEORY-871](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-871.md) and [CLAIM-160](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md).

- **29 readings went Active.** About half were narrowed first.
- **Seven were kept.**
  - [THEORY-339](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-339.md), 355, 359 and 476 assert general claims.
  - [THEORY-777](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md)'s condition disputes the study's noise floor.
  - [THEORY-277](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md)'s key lemma never closed. A reviewer wrote a new proof of it, which waits on a second checker.
  - [CLAIM-160](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) stays held: its objection [CLAIM-171](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-171.md) can be neither answered nor written in.
- **[CLAIM-471](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md) went Active** narrowed to "estimate". The stronger "establish" is a new interpretive claim, held until a case checks a measured correspondence against independent evidence.
- **The wider claims went beside their readings:**
  - 21 Proposed THEORYs where the source asserts the wider thesis;
  - 14 QUESTIONs where it does not.

**Titles that misstated their sources.** As in pass 22, reading to promote
found titles that said more than, or other than, their sources. Some
examples:

- **[THEORY-245](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md).** Posterior cortex carried identity for every category except
  faces, and one exploratory prefrontal site did respond at stimulus offset.
- **[THEORY-1120](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1120.md).** "Better than XCOMET" rested on 0.813 against 0.80, a
  difference that was not tested.
- **[THEORY-1051](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1051.md).** Its "only if" turned a sufficient condition into a
  necessary one.
- **[THEORY-480](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-480.md).** It said the court held that data sharing would restore
  competition. The court ordered the sharing and called the effect an
  expectation.
- **[THEORY-928](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-928.md).** It omitted the conditions its paper states, and without two
  of them the title is false. Separately, the paper's Eq. 11 is conserved
  only when the two temperatures are equal.
- **[THEORY-942](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-942.md).** Its own body said "only the converse is proved", but it was
  the converse that needed the unproved conjugation step.

**Re-derivations now written into the bodies.** Every proof checked here

## The owner's decisions on the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts", and what reading its twenty-one works changed in its argument: a counter to the world-model thesis, the SGD and self-distillation questions corrected, and the nucleation constructions put on a thermodynamic footing

*2026-10-31 15:27:48*

The owner answered the four questions the workbench entry of 08:48 left
open with "yes to all decisions and get started on those readings".

**The decisions.**
- **A term for "concept".** It is filed as Proposed, [TERM-098](../../record/terms.d/TERM-098.md),
  beside [QUESTION-360](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-360.md). The owner agreed there should be a term; it
  is not adopted, because the owner has not seen the definition.
- **Control theory.** It gets a topic, `control-theory` ([ADR-066](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-066.md)), applied
  first to the two control works and beside the existing tags of the
  viability and contraction entries.
- **[CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)'s title.** It is revised (version 3) to state a partial
  order of achievements rather than a nested sequence.
- **The five demonstrated claims.** They stay Active rather than waiting
  for a status review. The question was a choice between those two, and
  "yes" was read as keeping the first.

**What the readings changed** (curation entry of 15:27 for the readings
themselves). Each change below was made in place, under the entry's own
code, before merge.

- **The owner's world-model thesis meets its objection.** Richens et al.
  prove that across a family of composite goals a competent
  goal-conditioned policy fixes the transition function within a bound
  ([THEORY-1249](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1249.md)). They also say the map runs from the policy, so a
  lookup table over histories and goals has the same world model
  ([THEORY-1260](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1260.md)). Filed as a counter, Active and demonstrated:
  [CLAIM-513](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md).
  - **What it defeats.** The thesis's functional reading only. Its
    defeated_if is not met: the theorem compares no resources and
    intervenes on no internals.
  - **Where the thesis is out of scope for it.** The thesis's own setup,
    one interface without goals, is the myopic case the theorem excludes.
  - **What it corrects.** One item of the thesis: generalization within a
    family the table covers does not discriminate. [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) is
    revised to say so.
- **The SGD question loses one of its two sources.** Chen et al. deny a
  necessary relation between dynamical and Bayesian transitions. They do
  not conjecture coincidence, as the exchange and this record's first
  filing said. Their model gives a datum:
  - SGD's transitions have Bayesian counterparts in training order;
  - but SGD skips the 6-gon the posterior favours from n ≈ 600, so no
    single map from training time to sample size fits
    ([THEORY-1275](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md)).

  The maps the readings supply run from noise scale to sample size, in one
  basin ([THEORY-1255](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1255.md), [THEORY-1257](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1257.md), [THEORY-1258](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1258.md)).
  [QUESTION-363](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-363.md) is revised.
- **The self-distillation question's premise was wrong.** In Teoh's main
  setting the student sees what the teacher sees ([THEORY-1274](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1274.md)). The
  limit of a less-informed student is Hossain et al.'s ([THEORY-1259](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1259.md)).
  Mobahi et al. and Wu et al. are two different mechanisms of loss over
  rounds: a regularizer acting again, and fresh projections.
  [QUESTION-361](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-361.md) is revised.
- **The nucleation constructions on a thermodynamic footing.**
  - The reaction-network reader rewrote Construction 1 of [CASE-189](../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md) as
    reversible chemistry. Bistability needs about 3.52 RT of driving, and
    the case's equilibria are the limit of infinite affinity.
  - Maintenance costs current times affinity ([THEORY-1266](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1266.md)).
  - Chemostats are themselves finite-lived ([THEORY-1250](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1250.md)).
  - At finite size the maintained regime is metastable and is lost before
    the fold ([THEORY-1273](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1273.md)). Notes on [CASE-189](../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md) and [CLAIM-521](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md)
    record both.
  - [CLAIM-516](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) now states that its hypothesis is the limit of
    infinite affinity, and that its production graph is one of catalytic
    influence, not a stoichiometric cycle ([THEORY-1248](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1248.md)). Its proof
    stands.
- **The kinetic case's certificate** is robust invariance of the box, not
  Kolathaya and Ames's graded input-to-state safety. [CASE-190](../../record/cases.d/CASE-190.md) is
  revised.
- **Maximum entropy production.** [THEORY-671](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md) gets a note: in the Schlögl
  model the more stable state can carry either the higher or the lower
  entropy production ([THEORY-1270](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1270.md)).

**What the readings confirm.**
- A13's "a productive cycle need not be a stoichiometric cycle", in a
  stronger form.
- A16's description of Teoh's gradient routing.
- A20's use of Saligrama, which bears also on [CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md) and on
  [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md)'s sensor arm.
- A14's own caution that the SLT and thermodynamic exponentials are not
  one thing. LaMont and Wiggins's dictionary has no dynamics, and a
  posterior is the detailed-balance case, without circulation or steady
  dissipation.

**Corrections to the entry of 08:48, which is not rewritten.**
- Its line on A3 and Chen et al. ("their conjecture of the opposite")
  overstates the paper. A3 omitted the one-way conjecture and the shared
  direction.
- Its account of U15–U16 takes the exchange's less-informed student at
  face value for Teoh's setting.

**Left for the owner.**
- Whether to adopt [TERM-098](../../record/terms.d/TERM-098.md).
- Whether [THEORY-671](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md) should go to a status review on the Schlögl evidence.
- Whether [NOTE-293](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md) should cite Mandt et al. 2017 ([LIT-1898](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md)) now that
  it is held.

## The owner's review of the filing (2026-10-31, afternoon): three changes kept, five revisions made before merging, a synthesis note on will and correction, and a separate study of resolve against entrenchment

*2026-10-31 15:53:31*

The owner reviewed the pull request that files the exchange "Analyze
nucleation concepts", its readings and the decisions taken on it.

**What the review kept.** Three changes, singled out as particular
improvements:
- **[CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) as a partial order.** It corrects a tendency to present
  maintenance, reconstruction, inquiry and self-governance as a necessary
  developmental sequence.
- **The counter to the world-model thesis, [CLAIM-513](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md).** It separates
  whether a policy functionally determines a world model from whether a
  model is implemented as a component.
- **Finite driving and stochastic persistence** for the nucleation
  constructions. They strengthen the physical reading while limiting
  claims of indefinite maintenance.

The review praised the filing's "epistemic discipline", and in particular
the account of the adaptive reconstruction model's limits. Those limits
are the reserved allocation floors, the regularizer behind the copy rule's
return to fidelity, and the one-way coupling. They "identify the
mechanisms that a stronger future construction must endogenize."

**What was revised.**
- **The normative thesis, [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), version 2.** "A judgment about
  what is wrong need not specify what should be done about it."
  Evaluating a history, J_N(γ), is separated from fixing its admissible
  continuations, 𝒜_N(γ). The claim now holds only that judgments about
  continuity, reform and obligation can need diachronic relations that
  state descriptions miss. Prescription is a further question. The
  objection [CLAIM-512](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md), version 2, adds that distinction, conceded,
  and keeps its dilemma open.
- **The corrigibility study, [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md), version 2.**
  - Conditioning on a successful first correction selects different
    organizations across arms. So P(S₁ ∧ S₂) and P(S₂ | S₁) are both
    preregistered.
  - A branch starts every arm from a matched, corrected first-stage state.
  - Detecting the failure of the diagnostic apparatus itself is separated
    from detecting that an environmental hypothesis has failed.
- **The concept term, [TERM-098](../../record/terms.d/TERM-098.md), version 2.** Correctability comes out
  of the definition. An incorrigible concept is still a concept: a frozen
  classifier, an entrenched misconception, a rigid category. Mathematical
  concepts are corrected by proof, inconsistency or changed commitments,
  not only by what they are applied to. Conceptual corrigibility is a
  named further achievement, consistent with [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md). [QUESTION-360](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-360.md)
  gets the owner's negative control.
- **The world-model thesis, [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md), version 2.**
  - Compression and generalization support comparing architectures. They
    do not identify one, since many compact controllers are not explicit
    generative world models.
  - Establishing a mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate
    implementations, chiefly targeted interventions.
  - Richens et al.'s result is on the side of what a policy identifies.
- **Thermodynamic qualifications**, in [CASE-189](../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md) and [CLAIM-521](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md).
  - The 3.52 RT threshold belongs to one reversible network with chosen
    parameters.
  - At finite affinity the lower branch is low-activity, not extinct,
    since the reverse of decay is a basal production.
  - Pre-fold escape is not inevitable on every protocol. The hazard rises
    as the fold nears, and where the transition is observed depends on
    size, noise, horizon and sweep rate.
  - Three claims are kept apart: a deterministic saddle-node in the
    limiting model; possible escape before it at finite size; and an
    observed transition point that depends on the protocol.
  - The workbench entry of 15:27 says the regime "is lost before the fold".
    It is not rewritten; read it with this qualification.
- **Housekeeping.** The curation entry of 15:27 said twenty works were
  read in full and one skimmed. Two NOTEs are Skimmed, Chen et al. and
  Falasco and Esposito, so the count is nineteen and two; it is corrected.
  The changelog's `record/...` links were left as they are. Fragments are
  collected into the root CHANGELOG.md, where those paths resolve, as the
  review of 2026-10-27 established.

**What was added.**
- **Two notes on [QUESTION-364](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md)**, as synthesis and not as claims.
  - The first separates legibility ([TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)), volitional efficacy
    ([TERM-023](../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)) and correctability ([TERM-085](../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)), none of which justifies a
    demand. It sets the histories executable by an agent as it actually is
    against those that satisfy a standard. A nonempty intersection does
    not show the agent will choose well. An empty one does not exempt it,
    if its own earlier actions destroyed the capacities required.
  - The second records the owner's demand for a theory of historically
    situated corrective authority: endogenous governance ≠ historically
    continuous authorization ≠ legitimate authority.
- **[CASE-188](../../record/cases.d/CASE-188.md), a separate proposed study** of corrigible resolve against
  entrenchment. Two agents decide alike in ordinary conditions; one
  protects its commitment from irrelevant fluctuation and lets specified
  defeaters revise it, and the other grows better at enforcing it while
  evidence loses its way in. It is kept apart from [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md), which
  the review judged would otherwise become too complex to interpret.

The review's summary, kept as the larger lesson: "An organization can
maintain a commitment, recognize a reason to revise it, give that reason
practical authority, and execute a revision. These are different
achievements. Whether the commitment should persist, whether the reason
is justified, and whether the revision is legitimately authorized are
further questions."

## At the owner's question "no ARGs?": the filing's one verdict on support split out under ADR-061, and the synthesis on legibility, will and correction made a claim

*2026-10-31 16:01:04*

The owner asked of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation
concepts": "no ARGs?" The owner also said the synthesis on legibility,
volition and correctability "should probably be a new CLAIM, not hidden
inside the prose of a QUESTION".

**The ARG question.** [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md) puts in an ARG what the record says about
support between its entries; "X does not show Y" is the ARG from X to Y.
Every claim filed from the exchange was checked against that rule.

- **[CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md)** was a verdict on support. It said the record's
  constructions of corrigibility do not establish that it ought to be
  kept, and it had a subject-matter half beside that. It is split, as
  [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md) says a mixed claim is:
  - **[ARG-042](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md)**, Rejected, form `evidence`, holds the verdict. Its premises
    are [CASE-161](../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md), [CASE-162](../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md), [CASE-190](../../record/cases.d/CASE-190.md), [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md) and [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md).
    The question that fails is whether the measure measures what it is
    said to: every measure is of capacity, none of value.
  - **[CLAIM-520](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md)**, demonstrated and Active, is the subject-matter half:
    corrigibility's value is conditional, from A24's model. It
    `undercuts` the ARG.
  - **[CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md)**, version 2, is now the bare proposition, disclaimed
    and Proposed, as the ARG's conclusion.
- **The other claims stay claims.** They are about their subject matter:
  the fold, the provenance result, acyclic production, viable
  connectivity, distillation and viability, the normative thesis and its
  objection.
- **One borderline case.** The world-model thesis, [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md), says
  competent behaviour "does not establish" an internal world model, which
  reads like a verdict on support. Its content is a demonstrated
  observational equivalence, a fact about agents and their interfaces,
  and its premises are not record entries. It stays a claim.
- **Not filed as ARGs.**
  - [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md)'s "what would tell the accounts apart" is prospective,
    so there is no verdict to file until the study is run.
  - The owner's U20 point, that the order an inquiry met the achievements
    is no dependency order, has premises that are not record entries. It
    stays a note on [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md).

**The synthesis.** It is filed as [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md), a Proposed interpretive thesis
that uses [TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md), [TERM-023](../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md) and [TERM-085](../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md). It extends [CLAIM-349](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s split of
access, authority and action from an organization's own signals to
normative demands. The dated note on [QUESTION-364](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md) now points to it.
The note on historically situated authority stays on the question, since
it is a question.

## The owner's second review (2026-10-31, evening): "world model" names several things; a question that separates them, the owner's formulation and a general principle as claims, and a proposed study

*2026-10-31 16:21:59*

The owner's second review of the pull request judged it "substantively
close to merge-ready". It found the more interesting opportunity in the
world-model disagreement: "The current world-model debate is attempting to
adjudicate whether something exists before establishing which kind of
thing the term names."

**What was filed.**
- **[QUESTION-362](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-362.md), a question.** It separates five notions of world model
  (explanatory, behaviourally encoded, world-modeling competence, realized
  mechanism, self-maintaining modeling organization), with what would
  establish each. It also carries the owner's four counterexamples: a
  reactive controller, a full lookup policy, an unused simulator, and a
  distributed predictive controller. It extends [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md)'s three senses
  from Safron et al.
- **[CLAIM-514](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md), the owner's preferred formulation, as a Proposed claim.**
  World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded, query-relative
  capabilities, defined by a single implementable procedure meeting a
  loss bound within budget and deadline. A representational world model
  is one realization of them. It rests on both [CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) and its
  counter [CLAIM-513](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md), reading each as about its own notion:
  recoverability from a policy is not the agent's own access.
- **[CLAIM-515](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md), the general principle, as a Proposed claim.** Whether an
  organization has a cognitive property is four questions: what is
  recoverable from its behaviour, what it can exercise, what realizes it,
  and whether it can maintain or transform that. Following the owner's
  word at the previous round, that a synthesis belongs in a claim and not
  in prose, both are filed as claims, with the record's instances listed.
- **[CASE-187](../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md), the owner's proposed study.** Three architectures matched on goal
  competence are compared on goals, on-demand queries, internal
  interventions, and damage, under matched resources.

**What was revised.**
- **[CLAIM-519](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md).** "Not evidence" becomes "not sufficient to establish".
  The equivalence shows that competence does not establish or identify a
  model, not that it gives no evidence for one.
- **[ARG-042](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md).** Its premises are now sorted into executed studies
  ([CASE-161](../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md), [CASE-162](../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md)), a construction ([CASE-190](../../record/cases.d/CASE-190.md)) and a proposed
  experiment not run ([CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md)). It had said the record "has built
  and run" all of them.

**Not done.** The owner advised against replacing the world-model thesis
and its counter with one broad definition: "Their disagreement is
productive, provided it remains clear which notion each concerns." Both
stand; [CLAIM-514](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) places them.
